thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: multiple GPU pods on gpunode-13 reporting CUDA OOM during inference calls. Auto-page to @oncall.
anna (oncall): I'm on it, pulling logs now. Any customer-facing errors?
eva (support): Several customers in eu-west reported 500s and model failures starting ~2156788990. Small spike in error-rate dashboards.
raj (runtime): initial logs look like alloc failures inside the runtime allocator despite free_headroom=~1.8Gi on the node. snippet from agent:```ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
node=gpunode-13 pid=8421 free_headroom=1934507008 requested=207618048
backtrace: alloc_block -> try_reserve -> cudaMalloc```
mike (infra): so headroom shows available but cudaMalloc still OOMing. could be fragmentation or reserved-block accounting mismatch.
jen (sre): do we have recent kernel/drivers changes on that host? mike: nope, last deploy was 3d ago. GPU drivers unchanged.
raj (runtime): looks like the runtime held several stale 'shadow' reservations for KV cache that weren't released after session termination. they still count as reserved in our allocator but not reflected in headroom metric due to reporting lag. leads to alloc blowups on larger requests.
anna (oncall): ok mitigation options? can we force reclaim without node reboot?
raj (runtime): yes — we have a reclaim endpoint for the allocator. curl to the control plane:```curl -X POST "http://localhost:9001/debug/reclaim?node=gpunode-13&force=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"``` that will attempt to compact/free shadow reserves and drop cold KV cache pages. may temporarily increase p99 latency for affected inference calls.
mike (infra): alternative: cordon+drain the node and migrate workloads, but that's heavier. we can try reclaim first.
jen (sre): can we reduce batch sizes / disable prefix caching on the hot routes as quick fallback? anna: yeah we can set a per-route config to scale down batching.
deploy-bot: Executing route patch:```redwood route update --route inference-prod --batch-size 1 --kv-cache-enabled false```
anna (oncall): applying reclaim now, running curl command. will post results.
raj (runtime): while reclaim runs, please throttle big requests with the rate limiter to avoid repeated large alloc attempts. anna: setting transient limiter to 30rps.
eva (support): notifying impacted customers that we're mitigating and may see brief latency blips. drafting message now.
anna (oncall): reclaim returned: "freed_shadow_reserves=1.2Gi reclaimed=980Mi errors=0". node memory reported usable again but we still saw a couple of quick OOMs while reclaim in progress.
raj (runtime): good. next step: trigger per-pod soft restart on the 3 impacted pods to let runtime reinitialize caches:```kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-worker -l node=gpunode-13```
mike (infra): doing a rolling restart of the 3 pods now. will monitor GPU alloc metrics.
deploy-bot: rollout restart started for 3 pods.
jen (sre): watch p95/p99 and cuda error logs for the next 10m. if errors persist, plan is to cordon and migrate node.
anna (oncall): p95 dropping back toward normal, error-rate stabilizing. eva: customers acknowledged update, one said degraded but acceptable.
raj (runtime): follow-up actions: 1) patch allocator to surface shadow-reserve counts to headroom metric (so metrics align) 2) add periodic background compaction for KV cache 3) add an alert when reserved_blocks > metric_headroom by >200Mi. I'll own 1 and 2.
anna (oncall): thanks. jen, mike — please coordinate if we need node-level remediation tomorrow. I'll file incident report and page owners.
jen (sre): will do. adding postmortem template and tagging runtime/infra.
eva (support): closing customer loop: sent status update + expected follow-up timeline.
anna (oncall): incident resolved for now. creating ticket: INC-215678-allocator-ghost for postmortem. assigning to raj. thanks all. :thumbsup:
